fault_line: Blockade that bites, or blockade that leaks? Washington says stay away; trackers say oil still flows -- who is actually stopped?

sections.what_happened: US NAVCENT said via the Joint Maritime Information Center on Oct 28: 'Due to the current geopolitical situation, vessels which do not need to transit the area are advised to remain well clear to avoid unnecessary delays,' and transiting vessels should plan extra time for 'increased traffic density and military blockade enforcement operations.' Neutral vessels with neutral cargo or in ballast sailing between neutral ports may be subject to questioning, visit and search to confirm intentions regarding the blockade (Straits Times, Oct 28). ST notes this is the first similar public notice since mid-July, when the US blockade of Iranian shipping began; ST adds that oil flows from the Gulf are near pre-war levels via shuttle/dark transits, while Iran's attacks on ships are at a wartime high of almost 30 in October. PORTWATCH BACKBONE: the newest IMF PortWatch snapshot (2026-10-26, STALE flag true) counted 4 transits through Hormuz on 2026-10-18, 7-day average 3.7 vs a 2025 baseline of 85.5/day (4.3% of baseline) -- an AIS-counted figure that does NOT capture dark/shuttle traffic, which is why tracker 'near pre-war' claims and the counted 3.7/day can both be cited only with their methods attached. Never present a claimant number as a counted one.
sections.what_verified: Straits Times (T3) single family carrying the NAVCENT/JMIC advisory; advisory text quoted verbatim. No second family retrieved for the Oct 28 advisory text itself.
sections.what_disputed: PortWatch AIS counts (stale, Oct 18) vs tracker 'near pre-war flows' claims measure different things (counted AIS transits vs dark/shuttle-inclusive flows); the Oct 28 advisory's trigger is unstated ('It remains unclear what prompted the advisory' -- ST).
sections.why_matters: HORMUZ-BY-THE-NUMBERS frame: NAVCENT 'stay away' advisory + stale counted 3.7/day vs 85.5 baseline + Nov 1 Sinokor deadline; show the method gap on screen.
sections.context: Background: NEW -- US Naval Forces Central Command advisory Oct 28 (via JMIC): ships that do not need Hormuz/Gulf of Oman transits should stay away; neutral vessels face questioning, visit and search; ST notes Iran ship attacks at wartime high of ~30 in October
